target_customer: Virtual primary care clinics and direct primary care practices whose patients need in-person vitals, labs and nursing, paid in cash
problem: Virtual doctors cannot take vitals, draw blood or run point-of-care tests. Brick Health offered walk-in facilities with a fixed menu of diagnostics and nursing at transparent cash prices.
business_model: Cash-pay fees per diagnostic or nursing service, ordered by a virtual provider
product_category: In-person diagnostics and nursing infrastructure for virtual care

founders.name: Colin McDonnell
founders.background_notes: YC profile describes him as an engineer, founder and open-source contributor.

technical_complexity.rationale: Ordering and results integration with clinician records is ordinary software; the difficulty is operating licensed clinical facilities.

defensibility.rationale: Lab and nursing services are commoditized and local, with no documented network or regulatory moat.

market_need_then: Virtual primary care depends on outside labs for vitals and bloodwork, a gap the company described; no spend or customer figures found.

branding.domain_note: brick.health, a .health domain; the site no longer resolves.

brand_strength.rationale: No press or brand material found. The name is confusable with RedBrick Health and other Brick companies.

outcome_analysis: Brick Health was a one-founder company that planned walk-in diagnostic facilities to complement virtual primary care, and YC lists it as inactive with the founder under former founders. No shutdown note, post-mortem or acquisition was found and the website no longer resolves, so the cause of the failure is not public and no failure factors are assigned. Only a $150K YC deal is reported.
notes: The website brick.health did not resolve from this session's network, which may be a network restriction rather than a dead site. The $150K figure rests on a single aggregator (Diffbot data via a search listing), recorded with date 2019 from the batch year. Directories disagree on founding year (2019 vs 2020) and HQ (Miami vs Cupertino). The competitor list is empty because search results had no dated rivals near the batch; Carbon Health appeared only in undated pages.
